content.speaker: Sarah Chen
content.text: Alright everyone, let's get started. The main topic today is our database strategy for the new recommendation engine. Marcus, can you walk us through the options?

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: Sure. We've evaluated three options: staying with PostgreSQL, migrating to MongoDB for the recommendation data, or using a hybrid approach with PostgreSQL for transactional data and Redis for the recommendation cache.

content.speaker: Priya Patel
content.text: I've been running benchmarks. The hybrid approach with PostgreSQL plus Redis gives us 3x better read performance for recommendations while keeping ACID guarantees for transactions.

content.speaker: James O'Brien
content.text: From an ops perspective, adding Redis adds complexity. We'd need to set up replication, monitoring, and failover. But it's manageable — we already run Redis for session management.

content.speaker: Sarah Chen
content.text: OK, I think the data is clear. We decided to go with the hybrid approach — PostgreSQL for transactions, Redis for recommendation caching. Marcus, can you own the migration plan?

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: Yes, I'll draft the migration plan. We should have this done by end of September.

content.speaker: Sarah Chen
content.text: Great. Next item — we need to deprecate the v1 API. Our analytics show only 3% of traffic still uses it, but those are some enterprise clients.

content.speaker: Aisha Kumar
content.text: We should give at least 90 days notice. I'll prepare the deprecation timeline and client communication plan.

content.speaker: Sarah Chen
content.text: Agreed. Let's set the deprecation date for December 1st. Aisha will handle the communication, and Priya, can you add sunset headers to the v1 endpoints?

content.speaker: Priya Patel
content.text: Will do. I'll have the sunset headers deployed by next Friday.

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: One more thing — we should also look into migrating our CI/CD pipeline from Jenkins to GitHub Actions. Jenkins has been flaky and the maintenance burden is high.

content.speaker: James O'Brien
content.text: I agree. Let's plan the Jenkins to GitHub Actions migration. I can start the proof of concept next sprint.

content.speaker: Sarah Chen
content.text: Sounds good. James, you're responsible for the CI/CD migration proof of concept. Let's review it in two weeks. Action item: James to complete PoC by September 8th.

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: Also, going forward, all new services must use OpenTelemetry for observability. No more custom logging solutions.

content.speaker: Sarah Chen
content.text: Yes, that's the standard going forward. Let's document that as an ADR. Marcus, can you write it up?

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: I'll have the ADR drafted by end of this week.

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: Today we need to finalize the approach for extracting the authentication module into its own service. David, what's the security assessment?

content.speaker: David Kim
content.text: The current monolith handles auth in three places — login, API keys, and OAuth. We need to consolidate these. My recommendation is to use a dedicated auth service with JWT tokens and centralized key management.

content.speaker: Priya Patel
content.text: JWT makes sense but we need to handle token revocation. I suggest we implement a token blacklist in Redis — it ties into our existing Redis infrastructure.

content.speaker: David Kim
content.text: Agreed. The plan is to use JWT with Redis-backed revocation. We also need to implement mTLS between services for the auth service communication.

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: We agreed to implement JWT with Redis-backed token revocation and mTLS for inter-service auth. David, you'll lead this. What's the timeline?

content.speaker: David Kim
content.text: This is a significant change that affects every service. I'd say 6 weeks minimum. We should target mid-October for the initial rollout.

content.speaker: Lisa Wang
content.text: From an SRE perspective, we need canary deployments for this. If the auth service goes down, everything goes down. I'll set up the canary pipeline.

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: Good point. Lisa, please have the canary deployment pipeline ready by September 15th. Also, we need a circuit breaker pattern — if the auth service is unresponsive, services should fall back to cached tokens for up to 5 minutes.

content.speaker: Lisa Wang
content.text: I'll implement the circuit breaker. Someone needs to write the runbook for auth service incidents too.

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: David, can you write the incident runbook? Let's have it before we go to production.

content.speaker: David Kim
content.text: Will do. I'll have the runbook ready by October 1st.

content.speaker: Aisha Kumar
content.text: We're here to discuss migrating from our custom CSS framework to a shared design system. Tom, what's the design team's recommendation?

content.speaker: Tom Chen
content.text: We've built a component library in Figma that covers 85% of our UI patterns. The decision is to build our own design system package using Web Components, so it's framework-agnostic.

content.speaker: Nina Gonzalez
content.text: Web Components have some gotchas with SSR. We should use Lit instead of raw Web Components — it handles hydration better.

content.speaker: Aisha Kumar
content.text: Good point. Let's go with Lit for the design system implementation. Tom, can your team maintain the Figma-to-code pipeline?

content.speaker: Tom Chen
content.text: Yes, we'll set up Storybook and keep Figma synced. The design system package should be published to our internal npm registry.

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: What's the migration strategy for existing apps? We have 12 frontend applications.

content.speaker: Aisha Kumar
content.text: We should adopt a strangler pattern. New features use the design system, existing pages migrate incrementally. Nina, can you create the migration guide and prioritize which apps to migrate first?

content.speaker: Nina Gonzalez
content.text: Sure. I'll have the migration guide ready by September 10th. I suggest we start with the dashboard app since it has the most users.

content.speaker: Aisha Kumar
content.text: We agreed to use Lit-based design system with strangler pattern migration. The design system v1 should be ready by October 15th. Tom owns the component library, Nina owns the migration guide.

content.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
content.text: One thing — we need to add bundle size monitoring. Someone should set up a size-limit CI check so the design system doesn't bloat over time.

content.speaker: Nina Gonzalez
content.text: I'll add size-limit to the CI pipeline. Should be straightforward.
